name: Question 18
problem:
Consider a function $f(t)$ such that its Laplace transform is $L{f(t)}=F(s)$ for $s>{s}_{0}.$ Suppose we wish to find $L{{e}^{2t}f(t)}.$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below. By definition of the Laplace transform, we can write 

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{2t}f(t)} & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{{field-1}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{{field-2}}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={{field-3}}\,\text{for}\,{{field-4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 18
?
Consider a function f(t) such that its Laplace transform is L{f(t)}=F(s) for s>s0. Suppose we wish to find L{e2tf(t)}. Select the correct options in the reasoning below. By definition of the Laplace transform, we can write

 
e−st⋅e2tf(t)
e−st⋅e−2tf(t)
est⋅e2tf(t)
e−st⋅e2f(t)
 
e−(s−2)t
e(s−2)t
e(s+2)t
e−(s+2)t
 
F(s+2)
F(s−2)
F(s)
 
s>s0−2
s>s0+2
s>s0
L{e2tf(t)}=∫0∞{(e−st⋅e2tf(t))(S0)}dt=∫0∞{(e−(s−2)t)(S1)}f(t)dt={(F(s+2))(S2)}for{(s>s0−2)(S3)}.
